title: Lever a jammed wood plug out of a 2-1/8 in hole saw through its side slots, turning the saw between pries
instruction: The wood plug from the last hole is stuck in this hole saw. Get it out so the saw is ready to cut again.
context: Carpenters (about 890,000 US jobs) and electricians (about 821,000) bore holes with hole saws as routine work, and 2-1/8 in is the standard bore for a door lockset. The cut plug often jams in the cup; slotted saws like this one are made so a flat screwdriver can lever it out through the side. Levering from one side only tips the plug crosswise and wedges it tighter: one hand has to hold and turn the saw so the pries alternate sides while the other levers.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the bench top. Stand: a pine 4x4 offcut, 8.9 x 8.9 x 10 cm, standing on end and screwed to the bench, centred at (24, 8). Its top end has a hole 1.4 cm across and 3.2 cm deep (square in the model; drilled round in a real build, the hex shank turns freely in either). Hole saw on its arbor (steel, 280 g in all, free to turn and lift): the arbor's hex shank (1.1 cm across flats, 3 cm long) stands in the hole, and the arbor body (2.5 cm across, 1.5 cm tall) rests on the post. The 2-1/8 in bi-metal cup (5.4 cm outside, 5.14 cm bore, 4.1 cm depth of cut, 3 mm back plate) is open side up, its back plate's top 11.8 cm above the bench, axis at (24, 8). A 1/4 in pilot bit runs up the axis, 6 mm proud of the teeth. Two slots are cut opposite each other, one facing -y (towards the right arm), one facing +y. Each slot has two steps 49 degrees of arc (about 2.3 cm) wide, either side of a 3 mm web: the lower step's ledge is 13 mm above the back plate's top, the higher step's 25 mm, both open up to 33 mm; seen from above, the lower step is on the clockwise side of each slot. Plug: pine disc 5.1 cm across, 1.75 cm thick (cut from 11/16 in pine board), 18 g, with the pilot bit through its centre, jammed in the cup with its front face flush with the tooth tips and its back face 2.35 cm above the back plate. Screwdriver (NVIDIA SimReady handTool_screwdriver_slotted_65mm_a01): flat blade, 22.1 cm long, handle 11 cm long and 3.8 cm across, 5 mm steel shaft, blade tip 8 mm wide, 120 g; lying on the bench along y, blade towards the saw, handle centre at (14, -12), blade tip at (14, 4.8). Distractors (SimReady, loose, not scored): a speed square (measurement_ruler_speedsquare_a02, 29.0 x 21.8 x 0.8 cm, aluminium, 150 g) at (42, 24), turned 90 degrees; a retractable utility knife (handTool_knife_retractableBlade_a01, 16 x 6.1 x 2.6 cm, 120 g) at (45, -17), turned 23 degrees; safety glasses (accessory_eyeglasses_a01, 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g) at (45, -4), turned -17 degrees. Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read from the plug's travel: how far its front face stands out past the tooth tips (real trial: a ruler across the teeth, or 60 fps side video against a millimetre scale). 1.0: travel at least 23.5 mm (its back face up to the pilot bit's tip, so it lifts free) with every fingertip point of both grippers (each finger's tip and 3 cm up it) outside the plug's cylinder grown by 2 cm, held 2 s; scored 1.0 from then on. Otherwise, the travel at the end of the trial: 0.75 at 17.5 mm or more (the back face out past the teeth), 0.5 at 11 mm or more, 0.25 at 6 mm or more, 0 below 6 mm. The saw, the screwdriver and the distractors are not scored, and nothing else ends the trial.
reset_notes: Each trial uses a fresh plug: bore a 2-1/8 in hole straight through a 17.5 mm (11/16 in) pine board with this saw and pilot bit, stopping as soon as the plug breaks free, and leave the plug in the cup with its front face flush with the teeth (press it flush with a block if it stands proud). Check that it stays in when the saw is held teeth-down and shaken; bore another if it falls out. Stand the saw in the post with a slot facing the right arm, and lay the screwdriver and the distractors on their marks.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies. Saw, slots, teeth, arbor, pilot bit, plug and post are primitives at the Hole Dozer size; slot steps are estimates. The blade-plug contact is code: overlap gives a force pair on screwdriver and saw, and the plug slides once it passes a 60 N hold (estimate) that falls as it comes out. One-sided pries tip it; 6 mm of tip wedges it. It stops at 30 mm instead of falling free. Screwdriver (fitted box colliders) and distractors are SimReady.
